name: sm-04-through-division
title: Through division — do the emulators hold across the cell-cycle discontinuity?
claim:
The load-bearing untested boundary of the whole investigation: every sm-0x
conclusion is conditioned on pre-division single-cell trajectories, because
sm-00 halts each rollout at division ("the single-agent assumption breaks once
daughters appear"). sm-04 extends collection to follow ONE daughter lineage
across a real division event and finds that the emulators which win within a
generation (linear best; the sm-03 rollout-loss NN) do NOT hold across it:
none represents the cell_mass halving. This is an informative negative that
scopes the emulator to within-generation validity.
question:
Do the linear and neural (rollout-loss) emulators of coarse growth, which
emulate a single generation well (sm-01/sm-03), continue to hold when a
trajectory crosses a division event where cell_mass halves and the chromosome
count resets — or is the cell-cycle discontinuity a hard boundary the
observable-view emulator cannot represent?

report.title: sm-04-through-division — emulators across the division discontinuity
report.evidence_quality: 6-seed lineages rolled to/through one division (tick 2526); 6-fold leave-one-lineage-out CV; teacher-forced one-step + autoregressive rollout
report.objective:
Extend sm-00's collection to continue across a division (follow one daughter
lineage across the reset), then apply the existing linear + NN emulators on
the through-division data and measure prediction error ACROSS the division
boundary vs WITHIN a generation, under the same trivial-baseline comparison
sm-01 uses.
report.setup:
code/sample_through_division.py reuses v2ecoli's own multigeneration lineage
machinery (workflow/lineage.select_carry_daughter + apply_carry_state) to
step past the division tick — a single Composite cannot be run() through
division (the Division step _remove/_add of the mother agent breaks the step
scheduler), so the surviving daughter's biological state is carried into a
freshly-rebuilt composite. 6 seed lineages, each followed across one division
(~tick 2526) plus a within-generation tail in the daughter; every 1-second
transition tagged within-generation vs across-division. code/eval_through_division.py
runs 6-fold leave-one-lineage-out CV comparing persistence / mean-delta /
linear / one-step NN / rollout-loss NN on cell_mass. Emulators are trained on
within-generation transitions only (the sm-00/sm-01 regime) and then tested
across the boundary they never saw; errors are teacher-forced one-step
(isolating the discontinuity from rollout compounding), normalized by the
within-generation cell_mass std. Coarse growth is smooth (sm-01), so the
emulator operates at dt=8 s (temporal subsample), shrinking each ~2600-step
lineage to sm-03 scale while keeping the halving as one clean transition.
report.result:
At division the true cell_mass halves cleanly (median daughter/mother ratio
0.498; number_of_oric 4 -> 2) at tick 2526, consistent across all 6 seeds.

6-fold CV, cell_mass, teacher-forced one-step nRMSE (within-generation vs AT
the division tick), plus autoregressive rollout nRMSE (within-gen vs
through-division):

  model          within-gen 1-step   division 1-step   ratio     wg-rollout -> full
  persistence        0.0105              3.58            342x        1.79  ->  1.75
  mean-delta         0.0013              3.59           2738x        0.16  ->  0.81
  linear             0.0006              3.59           6204x        0.10  ->  0.81
  neural (one-step)  0.0003              3.59          13100x        0.18  ->  0.85
  neural (rollout)   0.0038              3.43            892x        0.39  ->  0.81

Every emulator predicts smooth continued growth at the division tick: fed the
true pre-division mother state, each outputs ~+small (its learned per-step
growth delta) while the truth is a ~-50% jump. The one-step error at the
boundary is ~3.5 nRMSE for ALL models — thousands of times each learned
model's within-generation error (linear 6204x, one-step NN 13100x). The
best-within-generation models fail WORST at the boundary (largest ratio),
precisely because they are most confident about smoothness. Autoregressive
full-lineage rollout error jumps ~8x when crossing division (linear 0.10 ->
0.81); the rollout sails straight through the halving (true 2433 -> 1221 fg,
linear rollout 2337 -> 2341 fg).
report.interpretation:
The emulators are valid only within a generation. The observable panel
(mass + chromosome) carries no state variable that encodes "about to divide"
at the resolution needed to fire a halving on the correct tick, so a smooth
autoregressive emulator cannot represent the discontinuity — and a
supervised fit cannot learn it either (a secondary check confirmed that
ADDING the 6 halving examples to training does not help and corrupts the
within-generation fit). This is the same shape of result the investigation
already found for the high-dimensional panel (unlearnable from the observable
view): the cell-cycle boundary depends on hidden state the curated view does
not carry. It extends, rather than overturns, the investigation's scoping
conclusion — the cheap linear emulator remains useful WITHIN a generation and
is simply undefined across division.
report.decision:
FAIL (informative negative, not tuned away). The emulators do NOT hold across
division; the primary test (emulators-hold-across-division) is failed by a
~6200x boundary/within ratio. Rolling through division needs an explicit
division event/reset in the model rather than a purely autoregressive
observable emulator — which is exactly the motivation for the latent
encode-decode direction (see followup_proposals).

variants.name: follow-one-daughter-through-division
variants.perturbation: Continue each lineage across one division, following the '..0' daughter (carry-and-rebuild), instead of halting at division as sm-00 does.
variants.expected_contrast: A transition that spans the cell_mass halving (mother ~2x birth mass -> daughter ~birth mass), plus post-division within-generation steps.
variants.measured_contrast: cell_mass halves at tick 2526 (daughter/mother ratio 0.498), oriC 4->2; emulator one-step error at the boundary ~3.5 nRMSE vs ~0.0006 within-generation (linear), a ~6200x break.

tests.name: emulators-hold-across-division
tests.question:
Does the best within-generation emulator (linear) represent the division
discontinuity — i.e. is its teacher-forced one-step error at the division
tick comparable to its within-generation one-step error (ratio near 1)?
The emulator "holds" only if the ratio stays small (< 2).

measure.detail:
6-fold leave-one-lineage-out CV (dt=8 s, cell_mass). Linear emulator
boundary_over_within_onestep_ratio = median(division-tick one-step nRMSE)
/ median(within-generation one-step nRMSE) = 3.59 / 0.00058 = 6204.
A value near 1 would mean the emulator holds across division; 6204 means
it fails completely to follow the cell_mass halving.

tests.cites_note: Methodological capability test; the large ratio is an informative NEGATIVE (the emulator is valid only within a generation). Mirrors sm-01's convention of encoding a negative as a failed hypothesis test.

emulators-hold-across-division.detail: Linear boundary/within one-step ratio 6204x (NN one-step 13100x); every emulator predicts continued growth at the halving. Informative negative.

embed_visualizations.name: Through division — emulator rollout vs the cell_mass halving (interactive)
embed_visualizations.description: One held-out lineage's true cell_mass across a division vs each emulator's autoregressive rollout (the rollout continues to ~2340 fg while the true mass halves to ~1221 fg), plus within-generation vs division-tick teacher-forced one-step error per emulator. Every emulator, trivial or neural, fails to represent the discontinuity; the best within-generation models fail worst at the boundary.

conclusion_verdicts.claim: The linear/NN emulators that win within a generation also hold across a division event.
conclusion_verdicts.basis: Teacher-forced one-step error at the division tick is ~3.5 nRMSE for every emulator vs ~0.0006 (linear) within-generation — a ~6200x break; the halving (ratio 0.498) is never predicted.

conclusion_verdicts.claim: The cell_mass halving at division is learnable from the observable (mass+chromosome) view.
conclusion_verdicts.basis: Adding the division transitions to training does not help and corrupts the within-generation fit; the boundary depends on hidden cell-cycle state the panel does not carry.

conclusion_verdicts.claim: The cheap linear emulator remains useful within a generation.
conclusion_verdicts.basis: Within-generation one-step nRMSE 0.0006 and within-gen rollout nRMSE 0.10 — unchanged from sm-01/sm-03; the failure is specific to the division boundary.

falsifiability:
The negative reading fails (i.e. the emulator WOULD hold across division) if
the division-tick one-step error were comparable to the within-generation
one-step error (boundary/within ratio near 1). It is confirmed here: the
boundary error dwarfs the within-generation error for every emulator, trivial
or neural (ratios 342x-13100x). All 6 seed lineages divide at the same tick
with a clean ~0.5 mass ratio, so the boundary behavior is not seed-specific.

simulation_set.name: through-division-cv
simulation_set.details: Follow one daughter lineage across one division; 6-fold leave-one-lineage-out CV of the emulators, within-generation vs across-division (dt=8 s emulator).

decisions_needed.question: Given the division discontinuity is not representable from the observable view, should the surrogate model division as an explicit event (a learned or rule-based reset triggered by a cell-cycle indicator) rather than a purely autoregressive step?
options: explicit division-event reset in the emulator
keep the emulator within-generation-only and document the boundary
pursue a latent encode-decode model that carries cell-cycle phase
decisions_needed.recommendation: Pursue the latent encode-decode direction (below); it addresses both the high-dim unlearnability (sm-01) and the division boundary at once.

followup_proposals.title: Latent encode-decode surrogate carrying cell-cycle phase
followup_proposals.rationale:
Both open negatives in this investigation — the high-dimensional panel is
unlearnable from the observable view (sm-01), and the division halving is
not representable across the boundary (sm-04) — point to the same missing
ingredient: hidden cell state the curated observable view does not carry.
A latent encode-decode model (encode the broad state into a low-dim latent
that includes a cell-cycle-phase coordinate, roll the latent forward, decode
back) could (a) make the high-dim groups predictable and (b) represent
division as a learned reset in latent space (phase wraps; mass/chromosome
halve). sm-04's through-division dataset (with its spans_division tags) is
the natural first training/eval target: success = the decoded rollout
follows the halving at the boundary (boundary/within ratio near 1), which
every current emulator fails.

followup_proposals.title: Division-indicator feature ablation
followup_proposals.rationale:
A cheaper intermediate: add an explicit cell-cycle indicator to the panel
(e.g. replication/D-period phase, time-since-birth) and test whether the
linear/NN emulator can then fire the halving on the correct tick. If a
single phase feature restores boundary skill, it localizes exactly what the
observable view was missing.
